NODO Design System

A single source of truth for foundations, tokens, and the 128 production components that power NODO products — documented with real usage guidance, specs, and accessibility notes.

128 public components 3,500+ documented variants 16 color ramps Light & dark themes 13 categories

Getting Started

NODO is built around design tokens first, components second. Every color, spacing value, radius, and elevation used across the library is expressed as a CSS custom property (or platform-native token), so a single theme change updates every component consistently in both light and dark mode.

1. Start with tokens

Reference --nodo-primary, --surface, --spacing4 and friends rather than hard-coded hex values or pixel numbers. This is what makes theming and future rebrands non-destructive.

2. Compose, don't rebuild

Almost every screen can be assembled from existing bars, controls, lists, cards and templates. Check the catalog before creating a new one-off pattern.

3. Respect states & a11y

Every component ships documented states (hover, pressed, focus, disabled, error) and accessibility requirements. Implement all of them, not just the default state.

Color Primitives

16 base ramps, each spanning from a near-white 10 step to a near-black 100 step (plus true white/black on Neutrals). Click any swatch to copy its hex value. Primitives feed the semantic Color Scheme layer — never reference a primitive ramp directly from a component; always go through a scheme token.

Color Scheme

Semantic tokens are the only colors components are allowed to consume. Each resolves to a different primitive step in light vs. dark mode so contrast stays correct automatically when the theme switches.

--primary-emphasis #bceffb #062465 blue/20 | blue/100
--primary-container #f5fbff #113cbb blue/10 | blue/80

--on-primary-container #113cbb #bceffb blue/80 | blue/20

Opacity & Strokes

Nine opacity steps (10%-90%) are used for disabled states, scrims, and subtle overlays. Stroke widths are standardized at 1px (default), 1.5px (emphasis) and 2px (focus ring).

Elevation

Four elevation levels create a consistent sense of depth, each tuned separately for light and dark surfaces so shadows never look muddy on dark backgrounds.

elevation-1
Cards at rest, list rows
elevation-2
Raised buttons, chips on drag
elevation-3
Dropdowns, popovers, tooltips
elevation-4
Modals, sheets, dialogs

Component Reference

Full specification for every public component, grouped in catalog order.

Bars

Bottom Bar Standard

Standard bottom navigation bar with 3-5 tab items, active tab highlighting

6 variants · bottom_bar_standard

Reach for Bottom Bar Standard when your screen needs standard bottom navigation bar with 3-5 tab items, active tab highlighting. It belongs to the Bars category, which covers top- and bottom-anchored navigation surfaces.

Key features

  • Standard bottom navigation bar with 3-5 tab items, active tab highlighting.
  • Ships in 6 documented variants, combining state.
  • Built on the NODO token set — color, spacing, radius and elevation are all driven by variables, never hard-coded values.
  • Designed to compose cleanly with other bars components without custom overrides.

Variant dimensions

state

When to use

Use Bottom Bar Standard when the pattern above matches the user's goal on screen. For unrelated needs, check neighboring components in Bars or a different category before introducing a one-off variant.

Do

  • Keep Bottom Bar Standard persistent and in a fixed position so users always know where core navigation lives.
  • Limit Bottom Bar Standard to the primary destinations a user needs constant access to (3-5 items).

Don't

  • Don't overload Bottom Bar Standard with more than five destinations — move the rest into an overflow.
  • Don't hide or auto-collapse Bottom Bar Standard in ways that make core navigation hard to find.

Usage patterns

Typically anchored to the top or bottom of the screen and present across every screen in its scope (root, flow, or hero context). Combine with page-level content that respects the bar's safe-area inset so content is never obscured.

Content guidelines

Labels should be one or two words, sentence case, and instantly recognizable as a destination (e.g. "Home", "Cards", "Transfers").

ARIA role & attributes

role="navigation" with an accessible aria-label describing the bar's purpose (e.g. aria-label="Primary"). Interactive tab items expose aria-current="page" on the active item.

Keyboard interaction

Tab moves focus between interactive items in the bar; Enter/Space activates the focused item. Arrow keys move focus between tab items when the bar behaves as a tablist.

Focus management

Focus receives a visible 2px outline using --nodo-primary-light offset from the component edge; focus never moves unexpectedly when Bottom Bar Standard changes state on its own (e.g. a loader finishing, a timer bar counting down).

Screen reader

Meaningful state changes in Bottom Bar Standard are announced via a live region or updated accessible name/value — never conveyed through animation or color alone.

Touch targets

All tappable regions (tabs, icons, CTAs) meet the 44x44dp minimum touch target, with a --spacing2 hit-slop applied to icon-only targets.

Contrast

Text and icon content in Bottom Bar Standard maintains at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background (3:1 for large text and non-text UI elements), verified against both the light and dark token sets.

Content guidelines

Labels should be one or two words, sentence case, and instantly recognizable as a destination (e.g. "Home", "Cards", "Transfers").

ARIA role & attributes

role="navigation" with an accessible aria-label describing the bar's purpose (e.g. aria-label="Primary"). Interactive tab items expose aria-current="page" on the active item.

Keyboard interaction

Tab moves focus between interactive items in the bar; Enter/Space activates the focused item. Arrow keys move focus between tab items when the bar behaves as a tablist.

Focus management

Focus receives a visible 2px outline using --nodo-primary-light offset from the component edge; focus never moves unexpectedly when Float Bar changes state on its own (e.g. a loader finishing, a timer bar counting down).

Screen reader

Meaningful state changes in Float Bar are announced via a live region or updated accessible name/value — never conveyed through animation or color alone.

Touch targets

All tappable regions (tabs, icons, CTAs) meet the 44x44dp minimum touch target, with a --spacing2 hit-slop applied to icon-only targets.

Contrast

Text and icon content in Float Bar maintains at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background (3:1 for large text and non-text UI elements), verified against both the light and dark token sets.

Do

  • Use Button for a single, clear action per instance so intent is unambiguous.
  • Pair Button with a concise, verb-led label that describes the exact outcome.

Don't

  • Don't use more than one filled, highest-emphasis Button in the same view or group.
  • Don't disable Button without explaining why nearby, or leaving it visibly unreachable.

Usage patterns

Focus management

Focus receives a visible 2px outline using --nodo-primary-light offset from the component edge; focus never moves unexpectedly when Check Radio Group changes state on its own (e.g. a loader finishing, a timer bar counting down).

Screen reader

Meaningful state changes in Check Radio Group are announced via a live region or updated accessible name/value — never conveyed through animation or color alone.

Touch targets

Minimum 44x44dp hit target regardless of the visual size token used, achieved via padding rather than resizing the visible control.

Contrast

Text and icon content in Check Radio Group maintains at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background (3:1 for large text and non-text UI elements), verified against both the light and dark token sets.

Do

  • Use Notification to confirm the result of an action the user just took.
  • Keep Notification messages short, specific, and free of jargon.

Don't

  • Don't stack multiple Notification instances on screen at once — queue them instead.
  • Don't use Notification for information the user must retain — use persistent content instead.

Usage patterns

Surfaced in direct response to a user action or a system event. Never more than one blocking feedback surface at a time; queue non-blocking ones (snackbars, notifications).

Content guidelines

Lead with the outcome ("Payment sent"), keep to one sentence, and only add a follow-up action when it is truly necessary.

ARIA role & attributes

Time-sensitive or blocking feedback uses role="alert" (assertive live region); passive feedback (snackbars, toasts) uses role="status" (polite live region); loaders expose role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax, or aria-busy="true" when indeterminate.

Keyboard interaction

Dismissible feedback (snackbar, notification, coachmark) is reachable via Tab to its action/close button; Escape dismisses coachmarks and tooltips.

Focus management

Focus receives a visible 2px outline using --nodo-primary-light offset from the component edge; focus never moves unexpectedly when Notification changes state on its own (e.g. a loader finishing, a timer bar counting down).

Screen reader

Meaningful state changes in Notification are announced via a live region or updated accessible name/value — never conveyed through animation or color alone.

Touch targets

Dismiss and action targets meet 44x44dp; the surrounding touch area does not trigger accidental dismissal of unrelated content.

Contrast

Text and icon content in Notification maintains at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background (3:1 for large text and non-text UI elements), verified against both the light and dark token sets.

Usage patterns

Surfaced in direct response to a user action or a system event. Never more than one blocking feedback surface at a time; queue non-blocking ones (snackbars, notifications).

Content guidelines

Lead with the outcome ("Payment sent"), keep to one sentence, and only add a follow-up action when it is truly necessary.

ARIA role & attributes

Time-sensitive or blocking feedback uses role="alert" (assertive live region); passive feedback (snackbars, toasts) uses role="status" (polite live region); loaders expose role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax, or aria-busy="true" when indeterminate.

Keyboard interaction

Dismissible feedback (snackbar, notification, coachmark) is reachable via Tab to its action/close button; Escape dismisses coachmarks and tooltips.

Focus management

Focus receives a visible 2px outline using --nodo-primary-light offset from the component edge; focus never moves unexpectedly when Snackbar changes state on its own (e.g. a loader finishing, a timer bar counting down).

Screen reader

Meaningful state changes in Snackbar are announced via a live region or updated accessible name/value — never conveyed through animation or color alone.

Touch targets

Dismiss and action targets meet 44x44dp; the surrounding touch area does not trigger accidental dismissal of unrelated content.

Contrast

Text and icon content in Snackbar maintains at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background (3:1 for large text and non-text UI elements), verified against both the light and dark token sets.

Do

  • Keep Loader Otp messages short, specific, and free of jargon.
  • Give Loader Otp a clear dismiss or auto-timeout so it never blocks the interface indefinitely.

Don't

  • Don't use Loader Otp for information the user must retain — use persistent content instead.
  • Don't block critical actions behind a Loader Otp that can time out before the user reacts.

Usage patterns

Surfaced in direct response to a user action or a system event. Never more than one blocking feedback surface at a time; queue non-blocking ones (snackbars, notifications).

Content guidelines

Lead with the outcome ("Payment sent"), keep to one sentence, and only add a follow-up action when it is truly necessary.

ARIA role & attributes

Time-sensitive or blocking feedback uses role="alert" (assertive live region); passive feedback (snackbars, toasts) uses role="status" (polite live region); loaders expose role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax, or aria-busy="true" when indeterminate.

Keyboard interaction

Dismissible feedback (snackbar, notification, coachmark) is reachable via Tab to its action/close button; Escape dismisses coachmarks and tooltips.

Focus management

Focus receives a visible 2px outline using --nodo-primary-light offset from the component edge; focus never moves unexpectedly when Loader Otp changes state on its own (e.g. a loader finishing, a timer bar counting down).

Screen reader

Meaningful state changes in Loader Otp are announced via a live region or updated accessible name/value — never conveyed through animation or color alone.

Touch targets

Dismiss and action targets meet 44x44dp; the surrounding touch area does not trigger accidental dismissal of unrelated content.

Contrast

Text and icon content in Loader Otp maintains at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background (3:1 for large text and non-text UI elements), verified against both the light and dark token sets.

Do

  • Use Tabs to show clear, linear progress through a known number of steps.
  • Keep Tabs labels short so they remain legible at every breakpoint.

Don't

  • Don't use Tabs for an unknown or unbounded number of steps.
  • Don't let Tabs jump backward unexpectedly when a user has already completed a step.

Usage patterns

Used to orient the user within a multi-step or multi-view experience. Pair with a persistent way to go back and, where relevant, a way to jump directly to a specific step.

Content guidelines

Step and tab labels are short nouns describing the destination or stage ("Details", "Review", "Done") rather than instructions.

ARIA role & attributes

Tabs use role="tablist"/role="tab" with aria-selected; steppers and progress indicators expose aria-valuenow/aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax or aria-current="step" on the active step.

Keyboard interaction

Arrow Left/Right move between tabs or steps; Home/End jump to first/last; Enter/Space activate the focused tab.

Focus management

Focus receives a visible 2px outline using --nodo-primary-light offset from the component edge; focus never moves unexpectedly when Tabs changes state on its own (e.g. a loader finishing, a timer bar counting down).

Screen reader

Meaningful state changes in Tabs are announced via a live region or updated accessible name/value — never conveyed through animation or color alone.

Touch targets

Tap targets for tabs, dots, and step markers meet 44x44dp even when the visual indicator is smaller (e.g. an 8dp pagination dot).

Text and icon content in Tabs maintains at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background (3:1 for large text and non-text UI elements), verified against both the light and dark token sets.

Do

  • Keep Item List rows consistent in height and internal alignment within the same list.
  • Put the most important information in Item List first (leading position) for fast scanning.

Don't

  • Don't mix row heights or layouts for Item List within the same list without a clear reason (e.g. section header).
  • Don't bury the primary action of Item List behind a secondary menu if it's used frequently.

Usage patterns

Used to present homogeneous collections of items. Prefer virtualized/lazy rendering for long lists and group rows with section headers or dividers when the list mixes categories.

Content guidelines

Primary text is the item's name/identity; secondary text carries supporting metadata (date, amount, status) and should not duplicate the primary line.

ARIA role & attributes

Rendered as

  • inside a role="list"/"listbox" container; interactive rows (draggable, checkbox, controls) expose the nested control's own role and label the row via aria-label built from its primary text.

    Keyboard interaction

    Arrow Up/Down move focus between rows in a listbox context; Enter/Space activates the row's primary action; draggable items support keyboard reordering via Space to pick up and Arrow keys to move.

    Focus management

    Focus receives a visible 2px outline using --nodo-primary-light offset from the component edge; focus never moves unexpectedly when Item List changes state on its own (e.g. a loader finishing, a timer bar counting down).

    Screen reader

    Meaningful state changes in Item List are announced via a live region or updated accessible name/value — never conveyed through animation or color alone.

    Touch targets

    Full-row tap target (not just the label) with a minimum 44dp row height; trailing controls keep their own 44x44dp target inside the row.

    Contrast

    Text and icon content in Item List maintains at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background (3:1 for large text and non-text UI elements), verified against both the light and dark token sets.

    Content guidelines

    Headings are short and specific; supporting text adds one layer of detail, not a full description — the destination screen carries the rest.

    ARIA role & attributes

    Cards use role="group" (or a native heading + article landmark) with an accessible name from their heading; fully-tappable cards use role="link"/"button" as appropriate instead of nesting an interactive element inside another.

    Keyboard interaction

    If the whole card is actionable, it is a single Tab stop activated with Enter/Space; if a card contains multiple actions, each action is its own Tab stop in visual order.

    Focus management

    Focus receives a visible 2px outline using --nodo-primary-light offset from the component edge; focus never moves unexpectedly when Small changes state on its own (e.g. a loader finishing, a timer bar counting down).

    Screen reader

    Meaningful state changes in Small are announced via a live region or updated accessible name/value — never conveyed through animation or color alone.

    Touch targets

    Entire card surface (not just the CTA) is tappable when the card represents a single destination, respecting a 44dp minimum in the shortest dimension.

    Contrast

    Text and icon content in Small maintains at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background (3:1 for large text and non-text UI elements), verified against both the light and dark token sets.

    Usage patterns

    Used to structure page-level content — promotional, informational, or transactional — inside the main content area, respecting the page's spacing scale.

    Content guidelines

    Section and banner copy leads with the benefit or the ask, keeps to 1-2 sentences, and pairs with a single clear CTA when action is expected.

    ARIA role & attributes

    Content blocks that are structurally significant use role="region" with aria-label or aria-labelledby; purely decorative content (spot illustrations) is aria-hidden.

    Keyboard interaction

    Interactive content blocks (accordion headers, carousel controls) are reachable via Tab; accordion headers toggle with Enter/Space and expose aria-expanded; carousels support Arrow Left/Right.

    Focus management

    Focus receives a visible 2px outline using --nodo-primary-light offset from the component edge; focus never moves unexpectedly when Matrix changes state on its own (e.g. a loader finishing, a timer bar counting down).

    Screen reader

    Meaningful state changes in Matrix are announced via a live region or updated accessible name/value — never conveyed through animation or color alone.

    Touch targets

    Expand/collapse headers and carousel controls meet 44x44dp; swipeable regions also expose equivalent tap controls for accessibility.

    Contrast

    Text and icon content in Matrix maintains at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background (3:1 for large text and non-text UI elements), verified against both the light and dark token sets.

    Section and banner copy leads with the benefit or the ask, keeps to 1-2 sentences, and pairs with a single clear CTA when action is expected.

    ARIA role & attributes

    Content blocks that are structurally significant use role="region" with aria-label or aria-labelledby; purely decorative content (spot illustrations) is aria-hidden.

    Focus management

    Focus receives a visible 2px outline using --nodo-primary-light offset from the component edge; focus never moves unexpectedly when Alert Banner changes state on its own (e.g. a loader finishing, a timer bar counting down).

    Screen reader

    Meaningful state changes in Alert Banner are announced via a live region or updated accessible name/value — never conveyed through animation or color alone.

    Touch targets

    Expand/collapse headers and carousel controls meet 44x44dp; swipeable regions also expose equivalent tap controls for accessibility.

    Contrast

    Text and icon content in Alert Banner maintains at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background (3:1 for large text and non-text UI elements), verified against both the light and dark token sets.

    Usage patterns

    Used as the top-level scaffold for a full screen or modal. Compose smaller components (bars, buttons, list items) inside the template's designated slots rather than rebuilding structure from scratch.

    Content guidelines

    Template titles state the task in the user's words ("Confirm your transfer") rather than the system's internal name for the flow.

    ARIA role & attributes

    Modal-based templates use role="dialog" with aria-modal="true" and an aria-labelledby pointing at the template's title; full-screen templates use a landmark region with a descriptive heading.

    Keyboard interaction

    Focus is trapped within modal templates while open; Escape dismisses where appropriate; Tab order follows the template's visual reading order (title, body, actions).

    Focus management

    Focus receives a visible 2px outline using --nodo-primary-light offset from the component edge; focus never moves unexpectedly when Template Modal changes state on its own (e.g. a loader finishing, a timer bar counting down).

    Usage patterns

    Used as the top-level scaffold for a full screen or modal. Compose smaller components (bars, buttons, list items) inside the template's designated slots rather than rebuilding structure from scratch.

    Content guidelines

    Template titles state the task in the user's words ("Confirm your transfer") rather than the system's internal name for the flow.

    ARIA role & attributes

    Modal-based templates use role="dialog" with aria-modal="true" and an aria-labelledby pointing at the template's title; full-screen templates use a landmark region with a descriptive heading.

    Keyboard interaction

    Focus is trapped within modal templates while open; Escape dismisses where appropriate; Tab order follows the template's visual reading order (title, body, actions).

    Focus management

    Focus receives a visible 2px outline using --nodo-primary-light offset from the component edge; focus never moves unexpectedly when Template Story Collab changes state on its own (e.g. a loader finishing, a timer bar counting down).

    Screen reader

    Meaningful state changes in Template Story Collab are announced via a live region or updated accessible name/value — never conveyed through animation or color alone.

    Touch targets

    All primary/secondary actions in the template meet 44x44dp and remain reachable above the safe area on small devices.

    Contrast

    Text and icon content in Template Story Collab maintains at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background (3:1 for large text and non-text UI elements), verified against both the light and dark token sets.

    States

    awaiting inputvalidatingsuccesserror/retrylocked out

    Do

    • Keep Authenticator focused on a single verification step at a time.
    • Support autofill and paste in Authenticator so users are not forced to retype codes.
    • Lean on the existing 48-variant matrix instead of requesting a new one-off combination.

    Don't

    • Don't require re-entry of a code in Authenticator without a visible resend option.
    • Don't silently fail Authenticator — always state clearly why verification did not succeed.

    Usage patterns

    Used at sensitive checkpoints (login, payment confirmation, sensitive settings changes). Always provide a fallback verification method if the primary one is unavailable.

    Content guidelines

    Copy reassures without alarming ("Enter the 6-digit code we sent to ***-123") and always tells the user what to do next.

    ARIA role & attributes

    Authentication surfaces expose role="form" (or role="alertdialog" for biometric prompts) with clear labelling of each factor being requested; OTP digit inputs are grouped with role="group" and an aria-label describing the expected code length.

    Keyboard interaction

    Tab moves between OTP digit cells with auto-advance on input; Backspace returns focus to the previous cell; Enter submits once all digits are entered.

    Focus management

    Focus receives a visible 2px outline using --nodo-primary-light offset from the component edge; focus never moves unexpectedly when Authenticator changes state on its own (e.g. a loader finishing, a timer bar counting down).

    Screen reader

    Meaningful state changes in Authenticator are announced via a live region or updated accessible name/value — never conveyed through animation or color alone.

    Touch targets

    Digit cells and biometric confirm buttons meet 44x44dp; autofill from SMS/keychain is supported so typing is optional.

    Contrast

    Text and icon content in Authenticator maintains at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background (3:1 for large text and non-text UI elements), verified against both the light and dark token sets.

    States

    awaiting inputvalidatingsuccesserror/retrylocked out

    Do

    • Support autofill and paste in Input Otp so users are not forced to retype codes.
    • Give Input Otp a visible, honest countdown or retry affordance when a code can expire.

    Don't

    • Don't silently fail Input Otp — always state clearly why verification did not succeed.
    • Don't reset a user's progress in Input Otp after a transient network error.

    Usage patterns

    Used at sensitive checkpoints (login, payment confirmation, sensitive settings changes). Always provide a fallback verification method if the primary one is unavailable.

    Content guidelines

    Copy reassures without alarming ("Enter the 6-digit code we sent to ***-123") and always tells the user what to do next.

    ARIA role & attributes

    Authentication surfaces expose role="form" (or role="alertdialog" for biometric prompts) with clear labelling of each factor being requested; OTP digit inputs are grouped with role="group" and an aria-label describing the expected code length.

    Keyboard interaction

    Tab moves between OTP digit cells with auto-advance on input; Backspace returns focus to the previous cell; Enter submits once all digits are entered.

    Focus management

    Focus receives a visible 2px outline using --nodo-primary-light offset from the component edge; focus never moves unexpectedly when Input Otp changes state on its own (e.g. a loader finishing, a timer bar counting down).

    Screen reader

    Meaningful state changes in Input Otp are announced via a live region or updated accessible name/value — never conveyed through animation or color alone.

    Touch targets

    Digit cells and biometric confirm buttons meet 44x44dp; autofill from SMS/keychain is supported so typing is optional.

    Contrast

    Text and icon content in Input Otp maintains at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background (3:1 for large text and non-text UI elements), verified against both the light and dark token sets.

    Usage Guidelines

    Cross-cutting principles that apply regardless of which component you reach for.

    Consistency over novelty

    Prefer an existing component and variant to a bespoke one-off. The catalog's 3,500+ documented variants exist so teams rarely need custom UI.

    One primary action per screen

    Across buttons, cards and templates, keep exactly one highest-emphasis action visible at a time so users never have to guess what matters most.

    State completeness

    Ship every documented state (hover, pressed, focus, disabled, error, loading) for a component before shipping the feature that uses it.

    Theme parity

    Validate every screen in both light and dark mode — tokens make this nearly free, but visual QA still needs to happen in both.

    Patterns

    Common flows assembled from catalog components.

    Onboarding

    hero-navbar → template-onboarding-product-info → page-control → docked-buttons.

    Checkout

    item-checkout (list) → label-amount → text-field (promo code) → button (primary, filled) → template-confirmation.

    Verification

    authenticator → input-otp → timer → snackbar (success/error).

    Empty / error recovery

    empty-error-state → spot-error → button (outlined, retry).

    Dashboard overview

    heading → card/small (grid) → sparkline-chart → list-amount.

    Settings toggle group

    item-control (switch) → divider → accordion-group.
